drills.q: 'to eat' (먹다) in polite present -아/어요?
drills.hint: Consonant stem 먹- + 어요; meogeoyo

drills.q: 'to go' (가다) in polite present -아/어요?
drills.hint: 가 + 아요 contracts to 가요; gayo

drills.q: 'to do' (하다) in polite present?
drills.hint: 하다 is irregular: 하 + 여요 → 해요; haeyo

drills.q: 'ate' — past tense of 먹다 in -았/었어요?
drills.hint: Insert 었 before 어요; meogeosseoyo

drills.q: 'will eat' — future of 먹다 with -(으)ㄹ 거예요?
drills.hint: Consonant stem takes 을 거예요; meogeul geoyeyo

drills.q: 'to listen' (듣다) in polite present -아/어요?
drills.hint: ㄷ irregular: ㄷ changes to ㄹ; deureoyo

drills.q: 'water' in Korean?
drills.hint: mul — a single-syllable everyday word

drills.q: 'thank you' (formal) in Korean?
drills.hint: gamsahamnida; 고마워요 is more casual

drills.q: 'friend' in Korean?
drills.hint: chingu

drills.q: 'school' in Korean?
drills.hint: hakgyo

drills.q: 'delicious' (it's delicious) in Korean?
drills.hint: masisseoyo; opposite is 맛없어요

drills.q: Which particle marks the direct object after a vowel, as in 사과__?
drills.hint: 를 after a vowel, 을 after a consonant; 사과를

drills.q: Which subject particle follows a vowel-final noun, as in 친구__ 왔어요?
drills.hint: 가 after a vowel, 이 after a consonant; 친구가

drills.q: Which topic particle follows a consonant-final noun, as in 학생__?
drills.hint: 은 after a consonant, 는 after a vowel; 학생은

drills.q: How do you negate 먹어요 by placing a word before the verb?
drills.hint: Put 안 directly before the verb; an meogeoyo

drills.q: 'three' as a native Korean number (for counting things)?
drills.hint: set; becomes 세 before a counter (세 개)

drills.q: '10' as a Sino-Korean number (for dates and money)?
drills.hint: sip; native equivalent is 열 (yeol)

drills.q: How do you say 'hello' politely in Korean?
drills.hint: annyeonghaseyo — usable any time of day

drills.q: How do you ask 'How much is it?' in a shop?
drills.hint: eolmayeyo? — from 얼마 (how much)

drills.q: How do you say 'please give me this' pointing at an item?
drills.hint: igeo juseyo — 주세요 = please give
